display.title: Matzliach and the Mitzvah of Negel Vasser, Part 1
display.summary_short: Before he passes away, Matzliach's father asks him to choose one mitzvah to keep with mesiras nefesh. He chooses negel vasser, and the storyteller teaches how to wash in the morning.
display.summary_long: In old Baghdad, Matzliach, the son of a wealthy scholar, learns in yeshiva and continues learning after his marriage with his father's support. Before his passing, his father hands over his business and passes on a family instruction: choose one mitzvah to guard more preciously than anything, ready to give everything for it, and in its merit Hashem will protect you. Matzliach chooses netilas yadayim of the morning, negel vasser. The storyteller then teaches the mitzvah: why we wash when we wake up, not walking four amos before washing, keeping the water by the bed, washing each hand three times in turn, first thinking of Hashem and saying Modeh Ani, and how the Frierdiker Rebbe showed the Chassidim how to hold their hands for Modeh Ani. He adds the Baal Shem Tov's teaching that the first thought, word and deed of the morning set the whole day. Back in the story, Matzliach prepares a two-handled cup each night, pours out the used water properly, and washes again before the morning brachos. To be continued.
display.lesson: Choose a mitzvah to treasure with all your heart; begin each day by thinking of Hashem, saying Modeh Ani and washing negel vasser properly.
